messages:
anya: Quick brain-dump — during a rolling model swap (v1 -> v2) we saw eviction storms for tenants with medium QPS. Thinking about an adaptive hysteresis that ties eviction aggressiveness to (1) recent miss rate, (2) per-tenant latency SLO breach flag, and (3) in-flight model-change flag. Thoughts?

sam: +1 on adaptive. Important: we need a safety cap so we don't balloon memory for long-tail tenants. Also how do we signal 'model-change' to all cache nodes atomically? 

kevin: For signal we used a short-lived epoch marker broadcast via controlplane. It's eventual, not atomic. Maybe treat model-change as a soft flag with ramp window 2m to avoid immediate policy flips. 

maria: Ramp window sounds right. Also, prefer decreasing eviction aggressiveness during swap so v2 gets more chance to warm. So hysteresis should be directional (less aggressive when model-change=true). 

dev-bot: deploy: model-swap/v2 started by @anya at 1768519990

sam: Edge case: tenant with hot keys — if we reduce eviction, hot keys might stay and block fair-share. Maybe combine with dynamic tenant credits so hot tenants can't hoard.

anya: Proposed config sketch:
```
evict_policy: adaptive_hysteresis
parameters:
  base_aggressiveness: 1.0
  model_change_multiplier: 0.5  # dampen eviction during swaps
  miss_rate_threshold: 0.05
  ramp_window_seconds: 120
  max_memory_overcommit_pct: 10
```

kevin: Looks good. One more: TL;DR for correctness — ensure prefix ownership handoff avoids double-claim races when we intentionally keep prefixes longer during swap. That touches lease/epoch logic.

maria: Agree — add a "handoff_grace" that's aligned with ramp_window and use the sequencer to serialize lease transfers where possible. If sequencer unavailable, fall back to idempotent-transfer that checks epoch.

anya: Ok action items: (1) spike on controlplane epoch broadcast + fallback (sam), (2) add tenant-credit limiter prototype (kevin), (3) sync with lease/sequencer owners for handoff_grace contract (maria). I'll open RFC follow-ups. Thanks :rocket:
